sources.note: Re-scores a search agent's own sampled tokens under a teacher that has been shown the instance's supporting evidence, and uses the detached teacher-student gap to nudge the GRPO advantage up or down on search and answer tokens only, without adding a distillation loss or changing anything at inference.
sources.title: EviSD: Evidence-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Agents

sources.note: Removes external supervision from on-policy self-distillation by building a pseudo-solution from the model's own majority vote and using it as privileged teacher context rather than as a scalar reward, then distilling only on the completions that disagree with it.
sources.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision

sources.note: Distributes hindsight supervision across the turns of an agent trajectory by comparing each turn's share of total revision magnitude against its share of eligible tokens, holding the average multiplier at one so the total supervision is fixed and only its allocation changes -- and isolates that allocation with a permutation control that keeps the multiplier values and scrambles which turn receives which.
sources.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Gives the teacher in on-policy self-distillation access to each completed student rollout and its verified outcome, adapting it to preserve behaviour on successes and redirect failures toward verified success, while the student keeps a prefix-only interface it can actually deploy.
sources.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

sources.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
sources.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

sources.note: Trains self-correction as a step-level preference problem -- preferring a detect-and-repair continuation over the continuation that would follow if the error went unaddressed -- after first initialising with ordinary step-level preference optimisation, and finds that correcting more often and detecting more errors both anti-correlate with accuracy.
sources.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs

sources.note: Gives a search agent an explicitly reversible trajectory tree with reflect and backtrack as first-class actions, and trains the reflection policy with a dense local signal distilled from a teacher that can see the whole trajectory alongside the sparse terminal reward the local decision is ultimately judged by.
sources.title: LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation

result.definition: The distance between what a teacher produces and what a student can reach, and across 7 sources the variable that determines whether a distillation method's reported gain is large or negligible. Its clearest measurement: one method's advantage over standard on-policy distillation is 1.0 point under weak mismatch -- inside the spread of three other baselines -- and 13.4 under strong mismatch, where the baseline is a model emitting 22K-token unterminated responses, so much of the strong-mismatch result is repair of breakage rather than transfer of reasoning. Two structural findings. There is a capacity floor: the same jury distillation that lifts a 12B student lowers a 4B one. And there is an idiom component distinct from capacity: a safety pipeline gains across one model family and loses utility across another, attributed to reasoning-style mismatch with the teacher's family rather than to size. The gap is also usable as a training diagnostic -- one source tracks it staying separated from zero with low divergence drift while a baseline's gap and drift both diverge as its success collapses -- and a formal result bounds what can cross it, since forward-KL distillation projects a trajectory-conditioned teacher onto its conditional mean, leaving the part that depends on unavailable information untransferable.
